summary: Polygon's Pete Volk and Toussaint Egan curate a list of excellent free movies on Tubi, Fox's ad-supported streaming service, spanning genres, cultures, and eras. The list features Planet Terror as the editor's pick, plus Certified Copy, Hoop Dreams, Joint Security Area, Mandy, Shadow, Steamboy, and What Lies Below, each with a short blurb. The piece will be updated over time with more Tubi picks.
one_line: Polygon recommends a curated list of great free movies on Tubi, from Planet Terror and Mandy to Certified Copy and Hoop Dreams.
key_facts: Tubi is Fox's ad-supported free streaming service with thousands upon thousands of movies.
Pete Volk found more than 100 of his "liked" Letterboxd films currently on Tubi while building the list.
Planet Terror, directed by Robert Rodriguez, is the editor's pick and was released alongside Quentin Tarantino's Death Proof as the double feature Grindhouse.
In Planet Terror, go-go dancer Cherry Darling (Rose McGowan) and El Wray (Freddy Rodriguez) survive a zombie outbreak caused by a rogue military commander played by Bruce Willis.
Certified Copy, directed by Abbas Kiarostami, stars Juliette Binoche and William Shimell and is set in Tuscany, where a French antique dealer meets a British writer.
Hoop Dreams, directed by Steve James, follows two high school basketball stars and is called the greatest basketball movie and one of the greatest American documentaries.
Park Chan-wook's Joint Security Area was the highest-grossing movie in Korean history at the time and helped launch the careers of Lee Young-ae, Lee Byung-hun, and Song Kang-ho.
Park Chan-wook's Decision to Leave was Pete Volk's No. 1 film of 2022.
Mandy (2018), directed by Panos Cosmatos, stars Nicolas Cage and has a score by the late Jóhann Jóhannsson; Cage named it one of his favorite movies on The Late Show With Stephen Colbert.
Zhang Yimou's Shadow is a wuxia film with political intrigue, a blade-made umbrella weapon, and black-and-white imagery in a color film.
Katsuhiro Otomo's 2004 steampunk anime Steamboy follows James Ray Steam in an alternate 1860s Britain and the "Steamball" invention.
Otomo's Orbital Era, his first anime feature in 20 years, was announced in 2019.
What Lies Below, directed by Braden R. Duemmler, stars Ema Horvath as 16-year-old Libby, who suspects her mother's new boyfriend John (Trey Tucker) is hiding something.
